ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached structure shows a cyclohexane ring. One ring carbon bears a chlorine substituent drawn with a solid wedge, and the hydrogen on that same carbon is drawn with a dashed wedge. The carbon across the ring bears a methyl group drawn with a dashed wedge, while its hydrogen is drawn with a solid wedge. Reasoning: The chlorine and methyl substituents are on opposite faces of the cyclohexane ring because one is shown as a solid wedge and the other as a dashed wedge, so the stereochemical prefix is trans. Number the ring to give the substituents the lowest locants; the substituted carbons are opposite each other, giving a 1,4-disubstituted cyclohexane. In the numbering tie, assign carbon 1 to chloro because chloro comes before methyl alphabetically. Therefore the name is trans-1-chloro-4-methylcyclohexane.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: it is a cyclohexane ring bearing Cl on one ring carbon and CH3 on the carbon across the ring. The Cl bond is drawn as a solid wedge while the CH3 bond is drawn as a dashed bond, so the two substituents are on opposite faces of the ring. Count around the ring from the chloro-bearing carbon as C1; the methyl-bearing carbon is C4. Apply alphabetical priority for the tie in numbering, placing chloro before methyl. Combine the stereochemical prefix with the parent name to get trans-1-chloro-4-methylcyclohexane.

The substituted ring carbons are opposite each other on the hexagon, giving a 1,4-disubstitution pattern.

In cyclic stereochemistry, substituents on opposite faces of the ring, one wedge and one dash, are trans.
